about: Game content for AER. Supplies, scrap and recipes are design values (marked 'values'). History cards and manual pages are factual except where they say 'game fiction'. Positions: pois.json.

materials.name: Metal
materials.note: Aluminium and titanium hull and frame pieces

materials.name: Solar cells
materials.note: Intact cells from a broken array

supplies.name: O₂ bottle
supplies.note: About 8.5 h of breathing at the daily-average work rate, 3 h at a hard walk

supplies.name: LiOH canister
supplies.note: 1 kg LiOH absorbs ~0.92 kg CO2 (2 LiOH + CO2 -> Li2CO3 + H2O): about 22 h at the daily-average work rate

supplies.name: Water pack
supplies.note: Drinking and evaporator cooling water. Cooling a 400 W walk uses ~0.59 kg/h (proposal §4)

supplies.name: Repair kit
supplies.note: Fixes one suit or equipment fault

rocketPieces.name: Tank and valves
rocketPieces.note: Leftover gas or water inside is random within the range

recipes.name: Storm shelter
recipes.does: Shelter anywhere: keeps gear out of the dust and cuts heat loss
recipes.catch: Heavy to carry (the materials weigh 17 kg) and slow to put up

recipes.name: Insulation wrap
recipes.does: Less heat loss at rest and at night

recipes.name: Cargo sled
recipes.catch: Slopes cost more, and it bogs down in soft sand (terrainClass 2 in layers_20m.json)

recipes.name: Solar patch
recipes.catch: Weak in a storm and loses output as dust settles; clear it to restore power

recipes.name: Oxygen tap
recipes.does: Recovers leftover liquid oxygen from a damaged tank as breathing O2
recipes.catch: Takes time, and only the oxygen left in that tank is recoverable

recipes.name: Direction finder
recipes.does: Gives a bearing to the rover's beacon

recipes.name: Rover comms link
recipes.does: Connects to the rover's radio to send the distress call
recipes.catch: Needed to win. Cannot be improvised without its manual page

improvise.rule: Any manual build except the rover comms link can be improvised without its page. A success counts as learned, so repeat builds use normal cost and time.

historyCards.title: Octavia E. Butler Landing
historyCards.text: Perseverance touched down here on February 18, 2021, lowered on cables by its rocket-powered sky crane. NASA named the spot after Octavia E. Butler, the science-fiction author who grew up in Pasadena, home of JPL. The rover's first drives studied the Máaz crater-floor rocks around this point.

historyCards.title: Wright Brothers Field
historyCards.text: On April 19, 2021 (sol 58), the Ingenuity helicopter lifted off here: the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. Under its solar panel it carried a stamp-sized piece of fabric from the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer. Ingenuity went on to fly 72 times before rotor damage on its last flight, on January 18, 2024, grounded it.

historyCards.title: Sky crane crash site
historyCards.text: After lowering Perseverance to the ground on nylon cords, the rocket-powered descent stage cut the cords and flew away so its crash would not hit the rover. It came down about 700 m to the north-west. The HiRISE camera on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed the V-shaped debris pattern days later.

historyCards.title: Parachute and backshell
historyCards.text: Perseverance's 21.5 m parachute opened at supersonic speed. Its red-and-white pattern hides two messages in binary code: 'Dare Mighty Things' and the GPS coordinates of JPL. Parachute and backshell landed together about 1.1 km west-north-west of the rover. Ingenuity photographed them from the air on its 26th flight, in April 2022.

historyCards.title: Heat shield impact
historyCards.text: The heat shield took the heat of entry into the Martian atmosphere, then dropped away during descent. It struck the ground about 1.5 km east-north-east of the landing site, where HiRISE spotted its impact.

historyCards.title: Three Forks Sample Depot
historyCards.text: Between December 21, 2022 and January 28, 2023 (sols 653-690), Perseverance set down 10 sealed sample tubes on this flat ground near the base of the delta: the first sample depot on another planet. It is a backup cache, in case the samples the rover carries cannot be collected later.

historyCards.title: Roubion: the sample that crumbled
historyCards.text: Perseverance's first coring attempt, in August 2021, ground the rock to powder, and the tube sealed nothing but Martian air. The team learned the crater floor here is softer and more weathered than expected.

historyCards.title: Rochette: the first rock core
historyCards.text: Two weeks after Roubion, the rover cored the harder rock Rochette and sealed Montdenier, its first rock sample, on sol 194 (September 2021). It is volcanic rock that water later altered.

historyCards.title: Séítah: rock from a cooling magma
historyCards.text: Séítah's rocks are rich in olivine crystals that settled out of a thick, slowly cooling body of magma. The rover cored the rock Issole here (samples Robine and Malay).

historyCards.title: Skinner Ridge: the first delta sample
historyCards.text: At the foot of the ancient river delta, Perseverance cored its first sedimentary rock, Swift Run, in July 2022: rock laid down by water flowing into the lake that once filled Jezero.

historyCards.title: Wildcat Ridge: organic molecules
historyCards.text: Wildcat Ridge is mudstone laid down as a salty lake dried out. The rover's SHERLOC instrument found organic molecules called aromatics in it. These are not proof of life, since chemistry alone can make them, but this is the kind of place where life could once have been preserved. Sample Hazeltop was sealed in July 2022.

historyCards.title: Observation Mountain: the first soil samples
historyCards.text: In December 2022 the rover collected its first regolith (loose soil) samples here, Atmo Mountain and Crosswind Lake. Soil samples help future astronauts understand the dust and grit they will live in.

scienceTarget.name: Wildcat Ridge
scienceTarget.why: Organic molecules found by SHERLOC in lake mudstone: the strongest science stop inside the map, and on the way from the crash site to the delta-front rover positions.
